questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Define the following

(i) Project (2 marks)

(ii) Critical Path (2 marks)

(iii) Milestone (2 marks)

(iv) Software Development Life Cycle (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Project (2 marks).** A planned set of related tasks carried out to achieve a specific objective, with a start and an end, within a given time, budget and set of resources.

**(ii) Critical path (2 marks).** The longest chain of dependent tasks in a project, from start to finish. It fixes the shortest time in which the project can be completed, and a delay in any task on it delays the whole project.

**(iii) Milestone (2 marks).** An important point or event in a project that marks the completion of a major stage or deliverable (for example the approval of the design). Milestones are used to check progress against the plan.

**(iv) Software Development Life Cycle (2 marks).** The series of stages followed to develop a software system, from the idea to its use and upkeep: planning and feasibility study, analysis, design, implementation (coding and testing), deployment and maintenance.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) An institution gradually replaces an old system in which workers write their names in an attendance register and the data is batch - processed weekly. In the new system, workers' fingerprints are scanned and registered automatically as a means to control presence at work. The institution runs both the old and new system for a while before the new system is finally adopted.

(i) What is meant by batch processing as used in the old system? (2 marks)

(ii) What type of processing does the new system use? (1 mark)

(iii) Give two reasons why the new method will be welcomed by the workers and administration. (2 marks)

(iv) What name is given to the type of changeover for the new system mentioned above? (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Batch processing (2 marks).** The attendance data is collected and stored over a period (here a week) and then processed all together, as one batch, at a set time without any user interaction, for example to compile the weekly attendance report.

**(ii) Type of processing (1 mark).** Real-time (online, immediate) processing: each fingerprint is recorded and the attendance record is updated at once.

**(iii) Two reasons (2 marks, 1 each).**

- It is fast and accurate: the attendance data is up to date at all times, with no weekly delay and no handwriting or copying errors.
- It prevents cheating, because a worker cannot sign for an absent colleague, so the administration can trust the records; the workers are also paid fairly for the time they really worked.

**(iv) Changeover (1 mark).** Parallel changeover (the old and the new system run side by side for a time before the old one is dropped).
